title: Synthesis, crystallographic study, Hirshfeld surface analysis,  in vitro  antimicrobial evaluation, and computational studies of novel pyrazole–isoxazole hybrid heterocyclic systems
content: A series of novel pyrazole–isoxazole hybrid heterocycles were synthesized using an efficient method and thoroughly characterized via NMR (1H, 13C) spectroscopy, HRMS and single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD). XRD and Hirshfeld surface (HS) analyses provided detailed insights into the solid-state structures, while DFT-based MEP and HOMO–LUMO analyses revealed stable electronic framework with defined interaction sites. The new compounds displayed significant antibacterial activity in vitro against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Among them, 6a showed the highest activity, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 50 µg mL−1 against S. aureus and 80 µg mL−1 against B. subtilis. Moreover, 6a exhibited important antifungal activity against C. albicans, A. niger, A. niger, and F. oxysporum, with MICs ranging from 5 to 8 µg mL−1 and a minimal fungicidal concentration (MFC) of 8 µg mL−1. Molecular docking indicated favorable binding of 6a to DNA gyrase B and lanosterol 14α-demethylase. Despite some ADME limitations, 6a represents a promising scaffold for further antimicrobial optimization.
